heading: INT. ICE CREAM FACTORY - ABANDONED - NIGHT

units.text: INT. ICE CREAM FACTORY - ABANDONED - NIGHT
A cavernous hall of frost-bitten steel.
Conveyor belts stilled mid-run.
Giant mixing vats, lids ajar.
A cracked pink sign reads "SWEET TOOTH CREAMERY - SINCE 1951".
Moonlight through a skylight.
The cold smells like old vanilla.
VIOLET ASHBY (40s, long coat, flashlight, a small digital recorder clipped to her lapel) steps over a fallen pallet.
She keeps her light low.
She keeps her shoulders square.
She stops at a cold-room door.
She puts her palm against it, as if she could feel a pulse.
She doesn't open it.
She moves on.
She finds a clipboard on the floor, wipes the dust with her sleeve, and reads for a long moment.
She tucks it under her arm.
She walks to the nearest vat, tilts the lid back with a boot, and shines the light inside.
Empty.
Dry.
Stained brown at the bottom.
Sweet Tooth Creamery. Tuesday, 2 a.m. No sign of forced entry.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: She lets the lid fall.
It echoes for too long.
She walks.
Her breath fogs.
Beneath her boots the floor changes, from concrete to a slick of old ice that crackles as she steps.
She slows.
She crouches.
She presses her glove to the ice.
Under the glaze, someone has frozen a wristwatch.
She stares at it.
Then she stands and takes four steps back, slowly, and lifts her head.
Along the far wall, a row of freezer doors waits in the dark, each with a small brass number.
One door is ajar.
A thin breath of fog curls from the gap.
She does not move toward it.
She does not move away from it.
Door nine is open.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: She plays the recording back.
Her own voice, tinny and small.
Door nine is open.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: Then, after a gap of dead air, another sentence she has not said.
Door nine is open, and you are standing in front of it.
units.name: VIOLET

units.text: She clicks the recorder off.
She stands there very still, her flashlight beam trembling on the floor.
She turns it, slowly, along the wall, row by row, door by door.
Eight.
Seven.
Six.
When the beam reaches door nine, it is closed.
She breathes out.
Fog drifts in front of her face.
She turns her back on the wall and walks, in a perfectly steady line, toward the exit.
Behind her, soft and unhurried, a latch clicks, and another, and another, down the line of doors.
She keeps walking.
She does not turn around.
Halfway to the exit she stops and unclips the recorder from her lapel.
She sets it on the floor, in the center of the aisle, red light still glowing.
She straightens her coat.
She walks on, and does not look back, and the recorder keeps running in the dark.
I'll leave this here. In case anyone wants to know how it ended.
units.name: VIOLET
paren: from the recorder, small and far off

units.text: The skylight fades to black.
